sources.notes: Official BMW M Motorsport page for the M Hybrid V8 LMDh (Dallara chassis, BMW P66/3 V8, 2023 debut). Used for real-world identity context.

sources.notes: BMW contrasts the road car's six-speed manual with the race M3 GTR's sequential transmission. Exact race gear count and actuation are supported by live testing.

sources.title: MCR Race Cars - MCR S2/02
sources.notes: Describes the MCR S2 as a mid-engined sports prototype running a Sports 2000 specification Ford Duratec two-litre of about 200 bhp, driven through a Sadev or Hewland five-speed sequential gearbox.

sources.title: Gearbox - Syncro vs Dog engagement
sources.notes: Technical comparison stating that a dog box needs perfect rpm selection by the driver or severe damage can be experienced, while synchromesh units make automatic adjustments to match gear and hub speeds. This is the basis for treating a downshift blip as required on a dog box and optional on a synchromesh gearbox.

sources.title: 2000 Oreca Viper, chassis C38
sources.notes: Includes a first-person account from Carsport Holland team principal Toine Hezemans that his team replaced the Oreca H-pattern gearbox with a Holinger sequential. Supports historical plausibility for a privateer sequential specification, but must not be generalized to every Viper GTS-R.

sources.title: Academy Championship
sources.notes: Caterham list the Academy car as road legal. The current page describes the later six-speed specification; road-legality is the constant of the formula and is what the gearbox construction is inferred from.

sources.title: Copa Truck - Regulamento Tecnico 2025
sources.notes: Official series regulations. Article 15 (CAMBIO) requires the gearbox to be coupled directly to the engine and states that the gearbox itself is free for all makes. Article 15.1a prohibits automatic and automated gearboxes and mandates a lever for a manual H-pattern change; 15.1b restricts the change mechanism to a rod or steel cable. The words sincronizado and garras appear nowhere in the document, so it fixes the gate and leaves the engagement type open by design rather than by omission.

sources.title: Anexo Tecnico Plataforma Stock Car Pro Series Car 2024
sources.notes: Official platform annex identifies the common prescribed steering wheel, pedals, transmission, and paddle-shift system used by the 2024 cars.

sources.notes: Official series regulations prescribe the Xtrac 396B023 transmission, semi-automatic paddle-shift actuation, and a multi-disc clutch. In-game technique is verified separately.

sources.notes: Specialist motorsport article identifies the period GTLM and its Hewland sequential gearbox. It does not establish gear count, actuation, technique, or wheel shape.

sources.notes: Specialist vehicle dossier identifies a Hewland TGTA six-speed sequential gearbox operated by a push-pull lever on a documented 2000 Storm GTM. It supports the hardware family but not every later chassis or the AMS2 technique.

sources.notes: Gives the competition Sigma P1 a 6.2-litre GM LT1 of about 600 bhp on a tubular chassis with an LMP3-derived XTrac gearbox, and the later G5 Evo a detuned 450 bhp engine and a Sadev unit.

sources.title: 2016 Dodge Viper specifications
sources.notes: Manufacturer press specifications identify the ACR's synchronized six-speed manual and ACR-specific sixth ratio. Gate and technique are supported by live testing.

sources.title: Puma P052 specs and price
sources.notes: Specifies the revived Puma P052 with a transverse rear 1,598 cc 16-valve four of 120 CV, a steel tubular chassis and fibreglass body, and a 5-speed manual, rear-wheel drive.

sources.title: Anatomy of a Le Mans GT car: the Ferrari 550 Maranello Prodrive
sources.notes: Technical account of the Prodrive-built 550 GTS Maranello: a six-speed Xtrac sequential with a flat-shift facility worked by an optical sensor at the base of the gearlever, a 5983cc V12 of 600 bhp, and racing in the FIA GT Championship from 2001 to 2005. States that the clutch is required for all downshifts and is not needed for upshifts when flat-shifting.

sources.title: Formula Vee 2025 Regulamento Geral/Tecnico
sources.publisher: Federacao de Automobilismo de Sao Paulo
sources.notes: Official 2025 technical regulations specify the Naja01-D Formula Vee chassis with a longitudinal Volkswagen Gol five-speed gearbox and defined clutch system. The following season's exact shift technique is established separately by live testing.

sources.title: FASP - Regulamento Desportivo Geral 2024, com anexos 1 a 6
sources.publisher: Federação de Automobilismo de São Paulo
sources.notes: Confirms Fórmula Inter ran under FASP's Paulista championship: page 38 carries "ANEXO 5 - FÓRMULA INTER". The complete annex is a "Tabela de Pontuação" and nothing else. It has no gearbox article, no prescribed, sealed or free rule, no ratio count, no donor unit and no synchroniser or dog field; those items are absent rather than negatively marked. This is a sporting regulation, not a technical one, and no published CBA, FASP or promoter technical regulation governing the 2015-2023 MG-15's gearbox was located.

sources.title: 575 GTC
sources.notes: Manufacturer page describing the 575 GTC and its 2005 evolution with a sequential six-speed transmission and multi-plate clutch. Reiza has not established that the fictional Milano GT55 is the Ferrari, so this is context only.

sources.title: FGA Copa Classic - Regulamento Tecnico 2024
sources.notes: Official series regulations, consulted through a third-party host. Article 8.1 requires a casing from the car or engine maker but allows it to be freely reworked and states the gears themselves are free - "Carcaca da marca do veiculo ou do fabricante do motor com livre retrabalho. Engrenagens: livres" - and 8.2 frees the differential. Category B also permits a more modern gearbox matched to the engine used. The category therefore does not preserve a car's original internals, so a car raced in it is no evidence of the road car's construction.

sources.title: Audi V8 Quattro homologation record 5409
sources.notes: Official FIA identity and homologation context for the Group A Audi V8 Quattro. Exact gate and simulator technique are established separately.

sources.title: Homologation form 670, Group 4: BMW M1
sources.notes: Homologated 2 December 1980, the M1's own Group 4 form and the one contemporary with the Procar series. Page 5 lists a ZF manual five-speed and two further five-speed ratio sets. It predates the article 603 layout and uses articles 92, 93 and 96 instead, which carry no synchroniser field at all, so the form is silent on construction rather than negative. It draws no gear-change gate. Neither of its two extensions carries a gearbox ratio table.

sources.title: Homologation form 240, Group B: BMW M1
sources.notes: Homologated 2 March 1983, after the Procar series ended. Article 603 names a ZF manual gearbox and marks every forward gear of both its five-speeds synchronised - the base set and an additional set, which share ratios with the earlier Group 4 form. Section 603 f) draws the gear-change gate with reverse above first and 1, 3 and 5 on the lower plane, a dogleg with first down and left. None of its seven extensions carries a gearbox ratio table, and no extension on any M1 form describes a Procar specification.

sources.title: Homologation form A-5327, Group A: BMW M3
sources.notes: Article 603 names a Getrag manual gearbox and tabulates two homologated five-speed sets, the base Handschaltung and an additional gearbox, with every forward gear of both marked synchro. Section 603 f) draws the gear change gate: reverse above first, with 1, 3 and 5 on the lower plane - a dogleg with first down and left. Later extensions homologate six-speeds of differing construction, including 12/08 VO whose synchro column is blank throughout and 38/20 VO which names a Hollinger without stating engagement. Extension 01/01 VO offers only a reinforced gearbox and gives no ratio table.

sources.title: Homologation form 3039, Group 3: Chevrolet Corvette Sting Ray LS6
sources.notes: Homologated 2 June 1971, contemporary with the 1971 Corvette AMS2 models. Page 9 records four forward ratios and states verbatim "Synchronised forward ratios: all four". Across the FIA's Corvette forms no four-speed is marked non-synchronised: 1966 form 523 and 1968 form 583 also state four synchronised ratios, while the 1962 and 1965 forms carry four-speed tables with no synchroniser field at all and are silent rather than negative.

sources.title: Chevrolet Corvette homologation form B-260
sources.notes: Official homologation evidence for a related C3-era Corvette, homologated 1984. Article 603 on page 6 has a synchroniser column and marks the Doug Nash four-speed synchronised on all four forward gears, with reverse not synchronised; the fifth-gear row is blank because the gearbox has four speeds, which is not a negative marking. It shows a floor-shifted manual with a conventional H gate and a hydraulic clutch. It does not uniquely identify Reiza's fictionalized C3.R Convertible or establish its exact control behavior.

sources.title: 2006 Formula One Technical Regulations
sources.notes: Official period regulations cap 2006 Formula One cars at seven forward ratios and regulate a driver-controlled clutch system. The exact R26 gear count and technique come from live testing.

sources.title: 2008 Formula One Technical Regulations
sources.notes: Official period regulations cap 2008 Formula One gearboxes at seven forward ratios and describe hydraulic gear-selection actuation. Exact R28 controls come from live testing.

sources.title: Homologation form number 5, Group GT2: Chrysler Dodge Viper GTS
sources.notes: Primary homologation evidence. Article 603 identifies a manual Borg-Warner T56 and lists six forward ratios. The associated FIA Historic Database entry records GT2 homologation from 1996 through 2010. This establishes the original homologated configuration, not every privateer conversion.

sources.title: Lister Storm homologation record and Homologation Form GT-008
sources.notes: Primary homologation form documents six manual forward ratios and period transmission extensions. It does not unambiguously establish the late GTM actuation or technique.

sources.title: Homologation form A-5269, Group A: Mercedes-Benz 190 E 2.3-16 (W 201)
sources.notes: Article 603 names a Getrag manual gearbox and tabulates two homologated five-speed sets, every forward gear of both marked synchro, and reverse synchronised as well. Section 603 f) draws the gear change gate: reverse above first, with 1, 3 and 5 on the lower plane - a dogleg with first down and left. Extension 26/22 VO, valid 1 April 1990, homologates a further five-speed with reinforced mountings and gear lever, every ratio marked synchr. The base sheet is headed 190 E 2.3-16; extension 29/02 ES carries the homologation to the 190 E 2.5-16/EVO II.

sources.title: Homologation form number 15, Group GT: Lamborghini Murcielago
sources.notes: Primary homologation evidence for the Murcielago competition identity. The extracted form does not clearly establish driver control technique.

sources.title: Saleen S7 GT Homologation Form GT-013
sources.notes: Primary homologation evidence for the Saleen S7 competition identity and longitudinal gearbox architecture. The visible form does not establish the exact AMS2 gear count, actuation, or driver technique.

sources.notes: Official category explainer specifies a manual H-pattern transmission for the current Formula Vee. It does not establish the AMS2 clutch, lift, blip, or wheel behavior by itself.

sources.title: F1 Glossary - Gearbox
sources.notes: Official championship explainer supports semi-automatic steering-wheel paddle actuation generally. Exact Renault model behavior remains grounded in the live AMS2 observations.

sources.title: How the 2005 Renault R25 finally ended Ferrari's dominance
sources.notes: Official championship technical history supports the R25 model identity and gearbox context. It does not independently establish the exact forward gear count or user-facing control technique.

sources.title: 2003 Corvette C5-R specifications
sources.notes: Archived General Motors specification listing a six-speed sequential-manual transaxle for the 2003 Corvette C5-R. It does not establish the exact year represented in AMS2 or driver technique.

sources.title: The five best Aston Martin racing cars
sources.notes: Reputable historical overview stating that most DBR9s used a six-speed sequential gearbox while some used H-pattern manuals. This supports the hardware family but requires exact simulator inspection to resolve the modeled variant.

sources.title: Formula Vee Technical Regulations - The Gears and Axle Drive
sources.notes: Section 3 requires that a fully synchromesh VW Type 1 or 3 gearbox must be used, with all four forward gears and reverse present and operative, and that the gearbox internals be assembled as originally intended by the manufacturer. Registered as corroboration that the category's air-cooled four-speed unit is a synchromesh one; it is an Irish championship and says nothing about the Brazilian five-speed Gol gearbox.

sources.title: Hybrid 101: Learn More about How LMDh Hybrid Power Works
sources.author: John Oreovicz
sources.notes: Official series overview of the common LMDh hybrid system, including the ability of an LMDh car to move through pits or paddock on electric power alone. Used to interpret the observed clutch-free move-off as hybrid launch behavior rather than a generic auto-clutch aid.

sources.title: Transmission/Gearbox/Shifting Types & Method
sources.notes: Official article used as the design target for the iRacing staging importer. No iRacing records are promoted in dataset 0.1.0.

sources.title: Lamborghini Diablo SV-R specifications and performance
sources.notes: Marque-specialist technical sheet for the 1996 SV-R. The only reviewed source that characterises the gearbox construction: "Lamborghini five-speed + reverse manual all-synchromesh". The synchro wording is explicit rather than a blank or a dash. It names ZF as the final-drive supplier, which is the final drive and not necessarily the gearbox. It states nothing about clutch use on running shifts.

sources.title: Lamborghini Diablo: celebrating 35 years of an icon
sources.notes: Manufacturer heritage data sheet. Specifies for the 1996 SV-R a 5,707 cm3 V12 of 397 kW / 540 CV, a "5-speed Lamborghini manual gearbox + reverse" and a "Dry, single plate" clutch. The same source lists the later Diablo GTR separately at 5,992 cm3 and 590 CV, so the two are not conflated and this record's identity is confirmed against the correct specification. The sheet carries no synchroniser or dog-engagement wording, names no gearbox supplier, and gives no running-shift instruction: those fields are absent rather than negative. It does not establish the dogleg gate.

sources.title: Huracan GT3 EVO2
sources.notes: Official model page establishes the exact EVO2 identity and provides cockpit and racing-wheel imagery. The parsed text does not independently establish clutch, cut, or blip technique.

sources.title: Lamborghini celebrates 10 years since maiden Huracan GT3 victory
sources.notes: Manufacturer history describes the Huracan GT3 lineage, including EVO and EVO2, with a six-speed sequential gearbox. Exact AMS2 actuation and technique are verified separately.

sources.title: Lamborghini Miura: The first supercar in history
sources.notes: Official Miura family history identifies the SV and a five-speed manual transmission. Exact SV gate and technique come from live testing.

sources.title: Revuelto digital brochure 2024
sources.notes: Manufacturer brochure specifies an eight-gear automated dual-clutch transmission. Exact simulator controls are supported separately.

sources.title: Lamborghini unveils SC63 hybrid racing prototype
sources.notes: Manufacturer announcement identifies the SC63 as an LMDh hybrid using the category's standard transmission architecture. Exact driver technique remains simulator-specific.

sources.title: Lamborghini Super Trofeo Europe 2022 Championship Brochure
sources.notes: Official brochure specifies an Xtrac six-speed sequential racing gearbox, Magneti Marelli electric actuator, lightweight flywheel, and racing clutch. Driver technique remains simulator-specific.

sources.title: Veneno Roadster technical specifications
sources.notes: Official model archive identifies the Veneno Roadster and provides cockpit reference imagery. A related Lamborghini history article specifies the seven-speed ISR architecture; exact AMS2 controls were tested directly.

sources.title: Ligier JS P217 technical specifications
sources.notes: Primary constructor specification identifies a Hewland TLS-200 six-speed sequential gearbox with semi-automatic pneumatic steering-wheel paddle shift. It does not establish launch-clutch technique, cut/blip strategy, or the exact wheel-rim category.

sources.title: Ligier JS P320 technical specifications
sources.notes: Primary constructor specification identifies an Xtrac 1152 six-speed sequential gearbox, semi-automatic pneumatic steering-wheel paddle shift, and Magneti Marelli gearbox/engine ECUs. Launch and cut/blip technique require separate evidence.

sources.title: Ligier JS P4 technical sheet
sources.notes: Primary constructor specification identifies a six-speed transverse gearbox, wheel-mounted selection, ZF centrifugal twin-disc clutch, and pneumatic shifts. It does not by itself prove AMS2 cut/blip behavior.

sources.title: Ligier JS2 R technical sheet
sources.notes: Manufacturer specification states a six-speed sequential gearbox, centrifugal twin-disc clutch, pneumatic paddle shift, and bespoke integrated-display wheel. Driver technique is established separately.

sources.title: O Mitsubishi Lancer Cup
sources.notes: Brazilian feature on the Lancer Cup. States the RS runs a "cambio sequencial de 6 marchas com powershift (trocas de marcha sem embreagem)" - a six-speed sequential with clutchless gear changes - at 340 cv. It mentions the R only as a discontinued class and gives it no specification.

sources.title: Lola B05/40, B05/42, MG EX264 specifications
sources.notes: Archived constructor-attributed specification stating that the Judd V8, Zytek, and AER turbo installations use six-speed manual sequential gearboxes. It does not establish paddle actuation, start technique, cut/blip, or wheel shape.

sources.title: Lola Heritage - T710 Corvette GTP
sources.notes: Chassis-builder heritage record for the Lola T710 that underpins the Corvette GTP. Used for real-world chassis identity context.

sources.title: Lotus Type 23
sources.notes: Lotus's own history of the Type 23, a purpose-built two-seat sports racer introduced in 1962 for FIA Group 4. States that gearbox choices typically included Renault or Volkswagen units, and that the Renault box was often preferred for its shift ergonomics in right-hand drive. Gives no gear count and names no Hewland option.

sources.title: Kit 718 GT4 Clubsport MR (982)
sources.notes: Manthey Racing's MR kit for the 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport. The kit revises aerodynamics and suspension and makes no powertrain change, so the six-speed PDK of the base Clubsport is retained.

sources.title: Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport MR (981), model year 2016 - Manthey brochure
sources.notes: Manthey's own brochure for the 981-based MR, consulted through a third-party host. Printed pages 6-9 itemise the MR vehicle and the retrofit kit: two-way racing suspension, adjustable front anti-roll bar, larger rear wing with reinforced adjustable supports, driveshaft spacer, brake-balance adjustment, carbon bonnet and doors, polycarbonate glazing, a 100-litre fuel system with rapid filling, a steering-wheel hub extension with additional wheel controls, a CAN gateway and data-logger interface, safety equipment, and an optional lightweight battery. The list contains no engine or gearbox modification, and Manthey's technical manual for the same car has no engine or gearbox conversion section - but neither states in words that the powertrain is unchanged. The kit does add controls to the wheel, which is why the rim's fittings are read from the homologation photograph of this exact car rather than from the base Clubsport.

sources.title: Maserati GranSport brochure
sources.notes: Archived original manufacturer brochure specifies the production GranSport's six-speed electrohydraulic Cambiocorsa gearbox, paddle controls, and simulated heel-and-toe. Race-car continuity is separately checked.

sources.title: Maserati GT2 Stradale - Racing is Life
sources.notes: Manufacturer model page specifies carbon-fibre paddle shifters and a carbon/Alcantara steering wheel with integrated shift lights. Exact gear count and simulator technique are supported separately.

sources.title: Il Tridente issue 32
sources.notes: Manufacturer magazine specifies the GT2 Stradale's eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. Exact AMS2 move-off and cut/blip behavior are supported separately.

sources.title: MC12 Versione Corse
sources.notes: Manufacturer comparison states that the MC12 GT1 used a manually operated sequential gearbox; the road-derived Versione Corse instead used electro-actuated Cambiocorsa. Gear count and technique are verified separately.

sources.title: Six Maserati MC12s in the FIA GT
sources.notes: Exact MC12 GT1 manufacturer technical data specifies a manual sequential gearbox with six forward gears plus reverse and a push-type carbon clutch. It does not state a driver rev-matching procedure or an automatic throttle-blip function, so neither blip field can be inferred.

sources.title: McLaren 570S GT4
sources.notes: Manufacturer customer-racing page for the 570S GT4: MonoCell II carbon chassis, 3.8 litre twin-turbo V8, and the Oerlikon Graziano seven-speed dual clutch Sequential Shift Gearbox whose electrically actuated wet clutches pre-select the next gear.

sources.title: Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16 Evolution and its DTM homologation
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the 190E 2.5-16 Evolution homologation specials: a dog-leg five-speed Getrag manual with first gear positioned left and rearward, deliberately moved out of the racing shift plane, with a limited-slip differential.

sources.title: Mercedes-AMG GT3
sources.notes: Manufacturer page for the AMG GT3 family: sequential six-speed racing gearbox mounted at the rear axle in transaxle configuration. The GT3 Evo is the updated version of the same car.

sources.title: Mercedes-AMG GT3 Manual B: Vehicle Operation, version 03
sources.notes: Publicly hosted copy of the original AMG Customer Sports vehicle-operation manual for the pre-Evo Mercedes-AMG GT3. Printed page 12 says the clutch does not have to be depressed while shifting in driving operation and 'only has to be operated when shifting from neutral to first gear.' Printed page 6 instructs the driver to depress the clutch and ease it in after selecting first. The document does not establish anti-stall or an automated launch clutch.

sources.title: 2016 Mercedes-AMG GT3 Race Car First Drive
sources.author: K. C. Colwell
sources.notes: First-person test of the exact original 2016 Mercedes-AMG GT3. The cockpit account states: 'There is a clutch pedal in this car, but it’s deliberately hidden because racers use it only to get the car moving.' It separately states that paddle shifts do not use the clutch.

sources.title: Mercedes-AMG GT4
sources.notes: Manufacturer page for the AMG GT4: a sequential six-speed racing gearbox in transaxle configuration on the rear axle, pneumatically operated with shift paddles on the steering wheel, behind the AMG 4.0 litre V8 biturbo.

sources.title: Metalmoro - MRX
sources.notes: Constructor page for the MRX customer prototype, successor to the MCR, with a 2016 chassis revision. It states the car accepts diverse engine and transmission options, so no single real-world gearbox is fixed; the AMS2 Duratec P4 is one such configuration.

sources.title: Classes
sources.notes: The championship's own class page. The JCW Class runs a Damico-tuned 2.0-litre turbo to a 255 bhp target through a Quaife sequential gearbox, with Nitron dampers and Alcon brakes.

sources.title: Classic Mini Gearbox
sources.notes: States the 3 synchromesh gearbox was fitted to all Minis between 1959 and 1968, with synchromesh only on 2nd, 3rd and 4th and first gear of the crash engagement type, and that a full synchromesh first gear arrived in 1968.

sources.title: Lancer Cup
sources.notes: Brazilian magazine feature on the Lancer Cup's R car, prepared from the Lancer Evolution X with fibre body panels, a safety cage, bucket seats and revised suspension. It does not describe the gearbox.

sources.title: Ginetta G40: race car buying guide
sources.notes: Describes the G40 with adjustable suspension, a five-speed synchromesh gearbox and a 1.8 Ford Zetec engine. Establishes synchromesh construction for the Cup specification.

sources.title: Dodge Viper GTS-R - Catch Me If You Can
sources.author: Don Sherman
sources.notes: Contemporary engineering report corroborating the production-derived Borg-Warner T56 six-speed transmission and documenting the race car's three-disc carbon-carbon clutch.

sources.title: NASCAR 75 Stock Car Evolution
sources.notes: Official series history supplies generation context and notes the Next Gen sequential shifter. It is not treated as proof that Reiza's fictional Gen1/Gen2/Gen3 labels map exactly to NASCAR generations.

sources.title: McLaren 720S GT3 (2019)
sources.notes: Reproduces McLaren's launch material for the 2019 720S GT3: a six-speed sequential paddle gearbox with a new electronic shift actuator, behind a race-prepared version of the McLaren M840T 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8.

sources.title: Caterham 620 R brings extreme to Goodwood
sources.notes: States the 620R uses a six-speed sequential gearbox with flat-shift behind a supercharged two-litre Ford Duratec of 310 bhp.

sources.title: Nissan GT-R NISMO GT3 2018 specification
sources.notes: NISMO customer-racing specification sheet: six-speed sequential transmission with semi-automatic paddle shift as standard equipment, VR38DETT twin-turbo V6.

sources.title: Nissan GT-R NISMO GT3 2018-Spec cockpit
sources.notes: Official exact-2018-Spec cockpit photograph. The wheel has molded side grips around a closed central control face, establishing the GT/Formula category; flattening alone is not used for classification.

sources.title: Nissan Heritage Collection - Nissan R89C
sources.notes: Manufacturer heritage record for the 1989 R89C: VRH35 3,496cc DOHC V8, chassis built by Lola Cars International after the switch from March Engineering, and a VGC five-speed transmission. It establishes real-world identity and gear count, not driver technique.

sources.title: Roco 001
sources.notes: Brazilian engineering write-up of the Roco 001. States it was built on the monocoque of a Ralt RT34 Formula 3 car by Robbi Perez and Jose Cordova for the P3 class, with a transversely mounted Suzuki Hayabusa motorcycle engine later taken to 1,500 cc and about 280 hp, driving the rear differential by chain rather than a shaft. It does not state the gearbox.

sources.title: ORECA 07 Media Kit
sources.notes: Primary constructor media kit specifies an Xtrac six-speed sequential gearbox and pneumatic steering-wheel paddle shift. It does not establish launch-clutch technique or simulator cut/blip behavior.

sources.title: Porsche 915 Gearbox vs G50 Gearbox, Porsche 911 3.2 Carrera
sources.notes: Air-cooled Porsche specialist comparing the two gearboxes. States that the 915 uses Porsche's own synchromesh design where the later G50 uses a Borg-Warner synchro. Describes the road gearbox family and does not address the race-specification 915/08 separately.

sources.title: Gear Sets and Dog Rings for Webster and Hewland Gearboxes
sources.notes: Catalogues dog rings as the engagement component of Hewland gearboxes, listing parts for the Mk-series and LD200. Establishes dog-ring engagement as Hewland's design approach, though it does not name the DG300 specifically.

sources.title: New Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport featuring natural-fibre body panels
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Official launch material for the 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport: a 3.8 litre flat six driving the rear wheels through a Porsche dual-clutch gearbox with six gears. A PDK has no clutch pedal, so the car cannot require clutch input to move off in the real world.

sources.title: Strong, swift, spectacular: the new 911 GT3 R
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Official launch material for the 2019 (991.2) 911 GT3 R: Porsche sequential six-speed constant-mesh gearbox with electronic shift actuator, changed by steering-wheel paddles.

sources.title: Porsche 911 GT3 R (991.2) cockpit
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Official exact-991.2 cockpit photograph accompanying Porsche's 2019-car launch material. It shows molded side grips around a closed central control face, establishing the GT/Formula category independently of the separate Cosworth display.

sources.title: Debut for the newest generation of the Porsche 911 GT3 R
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Official launch material for the 992-generation 911 GT3 R: sequential six-speed constant-mesh gearbox derived from the 911 GT3 Cup, with paddles driving an electronic shift drum actuator.

sources.title: Porsche 911 RSR (2019 model year)
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Manufacturer media guide for the 2019 911 RSR: a weight-optimised six-speed sequential constant-mesh gearbox in magnesium casing, shifted by an electronic actuator through steering-wheel paddles.

sources.title: Porsche 963 | Porsche Motorsport
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Official Porsche Motorsport page for the 963 LMDh (Porsche 9RD V8, spec Xtrac seven-speed, 2023 debut). Used for real-world identity context.

sources.title: Homologation form Nat-GT4-024: Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport MR (981)
sources.notes: The MR's own homologation dossier. Page 59 of 97 records "Clutch control system: GEARBOX CONTROL UNIT" and identifies a hydraulically actuated, normally-open dual clutch, so the clutches are worked by the gearbox ECU rather than by a driver. Page 88 of 97 carries a complete dashboard photograph showing the whole steering-wheel face: a continuous conventional rim, visibly flattened at the bottom, closed over the top, with conventional spokes and a few buttons, no control face spanning two dedicated hand grips, no wheel-mounted display and no wheel-mounted shift lights. The dossier does not state in prose whether a clutch pedal is fitted, and the absent wheel electronics are an absence in a photograph rather than a written negative.

sources.title: Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport (Typ 981), Model Year 2016 - vehicle description
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Porsche's own vehicle description for the 981 Clubsport, titled for model year 2016, consulted through a third-party host. Page 2 specifies a "Rigidly mounted six-speed PDK-gearbox (DCT, dual clutch transmission)". Page 3 names an Alcantara motorsport steering wheel with paddles and page 6 a GT4 instrument cluster with motorsport display elements - the display instrumentation is in the dashboard cluster, not carried on the rim. It does not state whether a clutch pedal is fitted.

sources.title: Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport world premiere, Los Angeles Auto Show
sources.notes: Official launch release for the 981 Cayman GT4 Clubsport, describing a modified six-speed Porsche double-clutch transmission operated by steering-wheel paddles. Independent of the vehicle description and agrees with it. Not to be confused with the 718 Clubsport launch of 2019, which is a different generation and is registered separately.

sources.title: Porsche Sprint Challenge Scandinavia - Sporting and Technical Regulations, 2021 Edition 01
sources.notes: Series regulations that treat the 981 Clubsport MY2016 and the 981 Clubsport MR MY2016 as one specification. Page 47 puts both under a shared power-transmission heading specifying "Six-speed Porsche Doppelkupplung (PDK)" with identical ratios, and pages 43-44 give both the same 385 hp engine. The 982 cars are listed separately immediately afterwards. This is what establishes that the MR kit leaves the powertrain of the base car alone: the regulations specify one gearbox for both, rather than any source saying the kit changes nothing.

sources.title: Gillet Vertigo - only remaining FIA GT chassis
sources.notes: Specialist race-car dossier documents a surviving 2005-period Vertigo with a Tractive six-speed sequential gearbox. It does not establish lever actuation, technique, or wheel shape.

sources.title: Le Mans 2010: Saleen
sources.notes: Specialist technical article specifying an Xtrac six-speed sequential transmission for a 2010 S7-R and stating that the type was introduced in 2002. It supports the family but does not prove the exact 2005 revision or technique.

sources.title: 2005 Spyker C8 GT2-R, chassis 046
sources.notes: Chassis-specific auction listing stating that the 2005 works car used a Hewland six-speed sequential gearbox. It does not establish actuation, technique, cut/blip, or wheel shape.

sources.title: Porsche 991.2 GT3 Cup Info
sources.notes: Gives the 991.2 GT3 Cup a 3,996 cc flat six of 485 hp at 7,500 rpm, a "Porsche six-speed sequential dog-type transmission" with "pneumatic gearshift activation (paddle shift)", and a triple-disc sintered metal racing clutch.

sources.title: Conheça o Fórmula Inter MG-15
sources.notes: Launch report for the F-Inter MG-15, naming the model and its constructor, Minelli Racing, and establishing Fórmula Inter as a real Brazilian category. On the gearbox it states "Produzida pela própria equipe técnica da Fórmula Inter, a caixa de câmbio conta com cinco marchas dispostas em 'H'" - a five-speed made in-category rather than a named donor production unit. It uses neither "sincronizado" nor "garras": the construction is absent rather than negative. It describes the gate only as an H, which neither corroborates nor contradicts a dogleg, and does not give first-gear position. No expansion of "MG" appears, so it is the model designation and must not be read as a person or a year.

sources.title: VW Transaxle
sources.notes: States the transmission gears are of the constant-mesh type with balk ring synchronizers, and places the 1st/2nd and 3rd/4th synchronizers on the pinion and main shafts. Establishes the Beetle transaxle as fully synchronized.

sources.title: Technical Data — REITER Lamborghini Murcielago R-GT
sources.notes: Constructor technical data specifies a Hollinger M6S six-speed sequential gearbox and a three-plate Sachs racing clutch. It does not establish driver technique or wheel shape.

sources.title: What gearbox does the formula trainer have?
sources.notes: Thread resolving the question for the Formula Trainer and Formula Trainer Advanced: a member who tested it states it is definitely sequential, and a Reiza internal tester explains that an H-shifter can still be bound to a sequential gearbox in game as an accommodation for players without sequential hardware, which is why the selection menu misleads. He also notes that Reiza does not state transmission specifications in the car selection menu.

sources.title: BMW M4 GT3 Media Guide
sources.notes: Printed page 5 compares the M4 GT3 and M6 GT3 directly: the M6 has a Ricardo six-speed gearbox and a hydraulic clutch. The page does not establish launch technique by itself.

sources.title: The systems that allow Alex Zanardi to drive the BMW M8 GTE
sources.notes: Printed pages 2-3 describe the fully automatic centrifugal clutch developed for Alex Zanardi's adapted BMW M8 GTE and previously tested in his specially modified M6 GT3. This is an explicit special-case boundary, not the baseline M6 GT3.

sources.title: What it's like behind the wheel of the BMW M6 GT3
sources.notes: First-person drive of the exact M6 GT3 says the car still requires a clutch to get moving and describes easing the clutch to pull away.

sources.title: Mercedes-AMG GT3 2020 Operations Manual R01
sources.notes: Exact 2020-car manual. Printed page 7 instructs the driver to press the clutch, engage first and ease in the clutch; page 13 limits clutch use to neutral-to-first, and page 14 documents ECU-controlled double-clutching on downshifts. It does not establish anti-stall or an automated launch.

sources.title: Mercedes-AMG GT4 Drivetrain Manual R1.0
sources.notes: Exact GT4 drivetrain manual. Printed page 73 of 112 instructs the driver to depress the clutch at idle, engage first immediately, and ease in the clutch. It does not establish anti-stall or an automated launch.

sources.title: Mercedes-AMG GT4 review: is it as scary as it looks?
sources.notes: First-person test of the exact AMG GT4 says the clutch is required when using first gear in the pit lane, corroborating the drivetrain manual's move-off instruction.

sources.title: The BMW M6 GT3
sources.notes: Official BMW media package includes dedicated cockpit and steering-wheel close-ups. It does not textually identify a wheel-mounted rev/shift-light array, so it cannot settle that field.

sources.title: BMW M6 GT3
sources.notes: BMW Motorsport customer-racing brochure mirrored by Iberian MPH. Printed page 2 describes a removable multifunction steering wheel with paddle shift and status LEDs, then identifies those LEDs with control/status functions. It does not establish a wheel-mounted rev/shift-light array.

sources.title: Ginetta G55 GT4 User Manual
sources.notes: Manufacturer manual mirrored by ManualsLib. Printed page 25 describes a steering-wheel scroll control operating the on-board digital display; printed page 29 documents automatic torque reduction and automatic throttle blipping. It does not place the display or shift lights on the wheel rim.

sources.title: Ginetta G55 GT4 Brochure
sources.notes: Printed page 6 lists steering-wheel-mounted controls separately from a driver display that includes RPM/shift lights. It establishes that the car has those cockpit functions, but not that either is integrated into the wheel rim.

sources.title: McLaren 720S GT3 Product Sheet
sources.notes: Exact 2019-car product sheet. Printed page 2 specifies a six-speed sequential motorsport transmission but contains no launch procedure or driver clutch-control instruction.

sources.title: McLaren 720S GT3 EVO
sources.notes: Manufacturer page for the exact Evo derivative. No customer operating manual or launch-clutch procedure was available from the page; original GT3 and GT3X behavior is not inherited.

sources.title: Saleen S7R First Drive
sources.notes: First-person drive of the 2001 Park Place S7R explicitly instructs clutch use on up- and downshifts and recommends heel-and-toe for braking downshifts. It supports manual blipping for the early S7R family but does not prove that every 2005 Xtrac revision retained the same procedure.

sources.title: BMW M6 GT3: 50 Years of Motorsport
sources.notes: The transmission engineer's own account of the M6 GT3 transaxle: a semi-automatic transverse unit with a sequential six-speed plus reverse racing gearbox in a magnesium casing, paddle shifted.

sources.title: Could This Be the Final Front-Engine V-12 Competition Ferrari Ever Made?
sources.notes: Chassis-specific specialist feature describing a six-speed Xtrac sequential stick and showing the cockpit of a Ferrari 575 GTC. It is contextual evidence only; it does not prove the fictional Milano mapping.

sources.title: 2005 Maserati GranSport Trofeo
sources.notes: Chassis-specific dossier with manufacturer correspondence states a six-speed paddle-shift automated manual and three-spoke Momo wheel. Exact modeled technique is tested separately.

sources.title: 1996 Chrysler Viper GTS-R, chassis GTSR C3
sources.notes: Documented chassis history and cockpit photography used as visual evidence for a round racing wheel. The restored early chassis does not by itself establish every late privateer detail.

sources.title: Porsche Cayman GT4 Clubsport first drive
sources.notes: Contemporary first drive of the 981 Clubsport, describing the car as operating "without a third pedal". This is the only reviewed source that states the absence of a clutch pedal directly; neither Porsche nor Manthey writes it, and neither documents a standing-start procedure.

sources.title: New SIGMA P1 G5 EVO, equipped with a SADEV gearbox
sources.notes: The gearbox maker's own announcement. States the EVO runs a SADEV six-speed sequential transaxle, the SLR90-20, with paddle shift, and that this is the first time the Sigma P1 has run a SADEV gearbox.

sources.title: Locally observed SimHub AMS2 car identity settings
sources.notes: SimHub 9.11.22 generated .shcarsettings files for locally observed AMS2 cars. The audit found 192 unique identities, with CarId equal to CarModel in every file. Used only to support exact observed telemetry names and explicitly reviewed aliases.

sources.title: Live AMS2 Formula telemetry identities observed through SimHub
sources.notes: Exact CarModel and CarId values emitted by AMS2 1.6.9.91 and observed through SimHub 9.11.22 during local live tests. The observed Formula identities were Formula V10 Gen2 (B) - High Downforce, Formula V10 Gen2 (M) - High Downforce, Formula Ultimate Hybrid Gen1 - High Downforce, Formula USA 2023 - High Downforce, Formula V8 Gen3 - High Downforce, and Formula Ultimate Hybrid Gen3 - High Downforce. These observations support identity matching only; control behavior remains verified against the separately versioned control source.

sources.title: Stadium Super Trucks chassis #22 nears completion
sources.notes: The series' own specification for the trucks it builds: a 2 or 3 speed transmission depending on track configuration, a 600 hp EFI V-8, 3000 lb, 104-inch wheelbase. It does not say whether the transmission is automatic and does not name the unit.

sources.title: Porsche 911 Carrera RSR 3.0 (1974-1975)
sources.notes: Describes the 1974 Carrera RSR 3.0 with the Type 911/75 flat-six of 330 bhp, a reinforced clutch and a five-speed gearbox carried over from the RS. It states no gearbox construction.

sources.title: Porsche 911 GT3 Cup (991) (2013 - 2016)
sources.notes: Gives the 991 GT3 Cup a 3.8-litre flat six of 460 hp at 7,500 rpm and "a six-speed dog-type gearbox developed by Porsche Motorsport which is operated via shift paddles at the steering wheel", noting it was the first Porsche brand trophy car shifted by paddles rather than a lever.

sources.title: Porsche 911 GT3 RSR (996), 2004-2005
sources.notes: Marque-specialist model history specifying a six-speed sequential gearbox with ignition cut for full-throttle upshifts. It does not establish actuation, start clutch, automatic blip, or wheel shape.

sources.title: 2008 Caterham Seven R500 Superlight
sources.notes: Lists a 6 Speed Caterham Gearbox and states the power is transmitted by either the standard six-speed gearbox or the optional Caterham Motorsport engineered sequential transmission.

sources.title: 10 Iconic Cars with Dogleg Transmissions
sources.notes: Secondary reference describing the dogleg layout and the cars that used it, including the BMW M1's ZF five-speed with first gear out of the natural shift plane.

sources.title: 1970-1980 Puma GTE
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the Brazilian Puma GTE built between 1970 and 1980: fibreglass body on Volkswagen running gear with an air-cooled flat four and a four-speed manual gearbox. Despite the GTE name it is a classic road-derived car, not a GTE-class racer, and AMS2 classes it under Copa Classic B.

sources.title: Manual stick shift system confirmed for Gen3
sources.notes: The championship's own confirmation that Gen3 cars retain the manual gear-change mechanism on the six-speed sequential transaxle, so the category is shifted by a lever rather than paddles.

sources.title: Touring Car Tyros: BMW E30 M3 and Mercedes-Benz 190E 2.5-16
sources.notes: Secondary comparison of the two Group A rivals, recording the E30 M3's Getrag 265 five-speed dogleg manual and limited-slip differential alongside the 190E's dog-leg Getrag.

sources.title: 2004 Birmingham Motor Show Press Information
sources.notes: Archived original manufacturer press kit connecting the T400R platform to the Le Mans program and describing a TVR six-speed sequential gearbox for the model family. It does not unambiguously establish the exact 2005 race-car technique.

sources.title: Why Your 911 lost its Dog-Leg Five-Speed Transmission
sources.notes: Records that the 915 replaced the 901/911 dog-leg first gear with a conventional H pattern, first up and left, citing a 1972 Porsche press release. Registered because secondary sources sometimes attribute the 901's dogleg to the 915, which would put first gear in the wrong place for any car running a 915.

sources.title: Porsche 911 Workshop Manual: Type 915 transmission
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Public scan of Porsche's period workshop manual. Printed page 283 introduces the Type 915 for 1972-onward 911s; printed page 284 says its five forward speeds and reverse are arranged in a double shift pattern. The reviewed text does not expose an exact 1974 Carrera RSR 3.0 selector diagram, so it supports the 915 family but does not alone close the RSR gate-layout question.

sources.title: FIA homologation form 3053: Porsche 911 Carrera RS
sources.notes: Homologation form 3053 establishes five forward synchronized gears and a lever on the transmission tunnel for the Carrera RS family. It is not a readable selector diagram for the Group 4 1974 Carrera RSR 3.0, so absence of a dogleg statement is not treated as a negative.

sources.title: Historie der Porsche 911 Carrera RS 3.0 / RSR 3.0 1974 und 1975
sources.notes: Exact 1974/75 Carrera RSR 3.0 account. Its power-transmission section says 'Das Getriebe war mit der RS-Ausführung identisch' and the technical table gives a mechanical five-speed Type 915. It does not provide a readable selector-layout diagram.

sources.title: Spyker C8 Spyder GT2-R specifications
sources.notes: Period-model specification and photo archive listing a five-speed manual, conflicting with the chassis-specific six-speed sequential source. The exact AMS2 modeled gear count and actuation therefore require direct observation.

sources.title: 5-Speed Gearbox Variants
sources.publisher: Westermann GmbH Motorsport, official partner of Caterham Cars
sources.notes: Lists the Type 9 five-speed in synchronized variants and one unsynchronized dog-engagement variant described as a motorsport application only purists find suitable for road use. Used as the falsifying alternative for the Caterham gearbox inference.

sources.title: Modern classic: Lamborghini Diablo SV
sources.notes: Describes the contemporary road Diablo SV as a "gated manual dog-leg five-speed". Establishes that the dogleg gate was the road car's own and not a racing modification, which removes the contrast the SV-R's gate was thought to draw. Says nothing about synchronisers or dog engagement.

sources.title: Copa Chevrolet Montana
sources.notes: Portuguese Wikipedia on the Brazilian one-make series, which ran from 2010 to 2012. Gives the cars a tubular chassis built by JL Racing, a carburetted Chevrolet 5.7 V8 of 350 cv, and a sequential gearbox. It does not state the gear count.

sources.title: Audi R8 (LMP)
sources.notes: Secondary summary describing a six-speed Ricardo sequential transmission with electropneumatic paddle shift. Retained as provisional historical context pending a primary technical replacement; simulator technique and wheel details are sourced separately.

sources.title: BMW 02 Series
sources.notes: States the 2002 turbo of 1973 to 1975 made 170 PS and that its gearbox was either a strengthened Getrag 232 four-speed unique to the turbo, or the Getrag 235/5 close-ratio five-speed also optional on the 2002 tii.

sources.title: BMW M1
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the M1 and its Procar racing version: a ZF five-speed manual whose first gear sits on a dogleg, placing first, third and fifth in the lower plane. The Procar used the same ZF DS25 unit with revised ratios and an added oil cooler.

sources.title: Brabham BT26
sources.notes: States that the BT26A switched to the Ford-Cosworth DFV and that both variants used a Hewland DG 300, 5-speed manual transmission with a ZF differential, raced from 1968 to 1971.

sources.title: Brabham BT44
sources.notes: Gives the BT44 a Hewland FG400 with 5 forward gears and 1 reverse behind the Cosworth DFV 2,993 cc V8, raced in the 1974, 1975 and 1976 Formula One seasons.

sources.title: Brabham BT52
sources.notes: Gives the BT52 a Brabham/Hewland 5/6-speed manual with a Weismann differential behind the BMW M12/13 turbocharged four, raced in the 1983 Formula One World Championship.

sources.title: Brabham BT62
sources.notes: Gives the Brabham BT62 a 6-speed Holinger sequential manual gearbox behind the 5.4-litre Ford Modular V8, in production from 2018.

sources.title: Caterham 7
sources.notes: Lists the Supersport (2011-2014) with a Caterham-Ford Sigma engine, and Seven transmissions as 5-speed manual, 6-speed manual and 6-speed sequential manual. The five-speed manual is therefore the non-sequential option.

sources.title: Caterham Academy
sources.notes: States the Academy package uses a sealed Ford Sigma engine and 5-speed gearbox, and that a six-speed Mazda MX-5 gearbox replaces it for 2026. Establishes the gear count, not the gearbox construction.

sources.title: Chevrolet Chevette
sources.notes: Brazilian Chevette built 1973 to 1993 with 4/5-speed manual gearboxes; a five-speed manual became available as an option on the 1.6 from 1983.

sources.title: Chevrolet Corvette (C3)
sources.notes: Records the C3 Corvette's four-speed manual in wide-ratio M20, close-ratio M21 and heavy-duty close-ratio M22 forms, standard from 1970 and available through 1981.

sources.title: Chevrolet Corvette C8.R
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the C8.R: naturally aspirated LT6.R 5.5 litre V8 and a bespoke compact Xtrac P529 six-speed sequential transaxle, packaged to free room for the rear diffuser.

sources.title: Chevrolet Corvette GTP
sources.notes: IMSA GTP prototype (Lola T710 chassis, Chevrolet power) raced 1985-1989; Hewland VGC five-speed racing gearbox. Used for real-world identity and gearbox context.

sources.title: Chevrolet Omega
sources.notes: Secondary reference for the Omega used in Stock Car Brasil from 1994 to 1999. The 1999 cars retained a heavily modified straight six derived from the 1979 Opala rather than the V8 introduced in 2001, and 1999 was the last season built on production-car chassis. It does not document the gearbox.

sources.title: Chevrolet Opala
sources.notes: Brazilian Chevrolet Opala, built from 1968 to 1992. Lists three-speed, four-speed and five-speed floor-shift manuals among its transmissions, without dating each, and records the car's endurance racing history against the Ford Maverick from 1973.

sources.notes: Brazilian racing-truck championship descended from Formula Truck. States the trucks have 1,000 horsepower, twice that of an average transport truck, and brake from over 200 km/h. sources.title: Courage C60

sources.title: Dallara SP1

sources.title: Lola T95/00

sources.title: The story of Porsche's RSR models: The best boxer in the motorsport ring
sources.publisher: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG
sources.notes: Porsche's four-page history identifies the first RSR as the 911 Carrera RSR 2.8 created for the 1973 season from the Carrera RS 2.7 to comply with FIA Group 4 (printed/PDF page 1). It distinguishes the 1973 2.8 from the later three-litre version (pages 1-2). On printed/PDF page 3 it states verbatim that the 'Ur-RSR' had a 'type 915 standard manual gearbox with five gears' and quotes Romain Dumas describing historical downshifts: the left foot used the clutch, the right foot worked brake and accelerator together, and 'Nothing worked without double-declutching.' It does not state the upshift technique or steering-wheel electronics.

sources.title: Porsche Carrera RS homologation form 3053
sources.notes: Official FIA consultation copy for Porsche Carrera RS homologation 3053 and its Group 4 extensions. Printed/PDF page 11 records a mechanically operated single-plate dry clutch, lever shifting, Porsche transmission type 911.300/08, five forward gears and five synchronized forward gears. Printed/PDF page 2 visibly shows three pedals, a floor lever and a conventional round continuous steering rim without integrated display or shift lights on the homologated Carrera RS base. The Group 4 extension beginning on PDF page 13 lists competition equipment including a steel-spring clutch disc, but it does not state driver technique or an alternate shift gate; absence from the extension is not treated as proof that no other racing variation existed.

The page does not specify the implemented gear count, gate, clutch behavior, cut, blip, or steering wheel, so those remain grounded in the fingerprinted guided drive rather than inherited from the marketing description.
